directives.name: The Siberian Mandate
directives.title: The Siberian Mandate
directives.desc:
After years of struggle the unthinkable has been achieved. The vastness of Siberia has been reunified under one flag. Securing this much of Russia has been no easy feat. To secure our hold we have had to fight off every devil of Russia's past, from monarchists fanatics to fascist thugs to Soviet holdouts. We have vanquished them all and we now stand triumphant as the masters of the east and the rightful government of all of Russia.

The conquest of Siberia has taken its toll on us. Russia remains fractured but even now we are already one of the largest nations on earth, and administering a territory this massive requires a strong and stable government. We should take this opportunity to secure our hold and ensure that our administration is prepared for the tasks that lie ahead. The final reunification with the west is near, one way or another. We will not be caught unprepared.

directives.name: Into the Atomic Age
directives.title: Into the Atomic Age
directives.desc:
Russia has long been regarded, by powers near and far, as a backwater, a vast steppe full of peasant farmers, and decades of revolution, collapse, and civil war has done little to challenge this perception. But this will soon change.

With the resources, human and otherwise, that we have acquired during our campaigns of re-unification, we possess the ability to begin a nuclear program.

The power of the atom is a great equalizer in the game of geopolitics, and we shall now act to harness it for ourselves.

directives.name: Root Out the Remnants
directives.title: Root Out the Remnants
directives.desc:
The Russian people are grateful to have a strong, democratic government ruling over them at last, but there are still a few troublemakers who wish to overthrow us. These various extremists, whether they be fascists or communists or anarchists or monarchists, are all unified by their hatred for our government. These radicals held low enough profiles to be missed by the first round of crackdowns and arrests we made whenever we defeated their bosses, but now they have returned to make trouble and we must put a stop to it.

There is no reason to assume what worked before won't work again. A combination of surveillance, sabotage, arrests, and anti-radical propaganda will be enough to cripple the various terrorist societies that have cropped up across Siberia and turn the public firmly against their divisive messages.

directives.name: Consolidate the New Territories
directives.title: Consolidate the New Territories
directives.desc:
It is almost impossible to explain just how vast and sparsely populated Siberia is. Outside of a few urban centers like Irkutsk and Novosibirsk, it is millions of square kilometers of wilderness and scattered villages. This is especially true of the newly integrated eastern regions. Even the Tsars and the Soviets never fully extended their administrations over this region, and the eastern warlords never came close to matching what they did accomplish. The task of integrating this territory has been left to us.

The urban centers of the east will form a nucleus of a new administrative web that will cover all of Eastern Siberia. Every town and village, every isolated hamlet, all of them will be assigned to districts and administrative regions, and each will have administrators and politicians appointed to oversee them and represent them within our government. No more will the Far East be an isolated backwater forgotten by the Russian government. It is an integral part of the Russian nation, and it will be treated as such.

directives.name: Reaffirm Our Commitments
directives.title: Reaffirm Our Commitments
directives.desc:
With the sudden expansion of our territory and our associated advance on the world stage, eyes across the world are studying us, watching for our next move to see what it signals. We must show them that we are still the same government they have learned to trust. Our impending reunification of Russia has not changed any of our agreements, and we are still happy to do business with the other nations of the world.

The acquisition of Russia's longest coastline and several developed ports has made the matter of trade much easier. The nations and companies who have already invested in Russia are excitedly offering to expand operations further. Meanwhile from Tokyo to Washington we have gained the attention of government and business alike. It is time to double down on our message while everyone is watching: Russia is open for business.

directives.name: Establish Closed Facilities
directives.title: Establish Closed Facilities
directives.desc:
Just as we are desperate to unlock the secrets of the atom, our enemies are equally desperate to prevent us from doing so. Although there are many ways to increase security, very few are absolute, and absolute security is necessary when the stakes are so high.

We will therefore sequester our entire nuclear program - laboratories, enrichment facilities, reactors, and production lines - in closed cities. These cities will not permit entry or exit to anyone without direct authorization from the highest levels of government.

Although cumbersome and expensive, such is irrelevant. We must have safety and security for the program, and we will.

directives.name: Address the Uranium Problem
directives.title: Address the Uranium Problem
directives.desc:
Russia is a truly enormous land, possessing many varied resources in vast abundance. Unfortunately, however, uranium is not one of those, so far as we know. Without a steady and reliable supply of uranium, we will have no program, and thus no bomb.

We must therefore make every effort in order to find this supply as soon as possible. No matter what it costs, we must find new sources of fissile material.

directives.name: Election Season
directives.title: Election Season
directives.desc:
It is no secret that the co-rulers of our nation do not get along. Publicly, Pokryshkin and Shukshin present a united front, but it is well known that they have agreed on little for years. The two men have been able to set aside their differences and cooperate up until now, but with the recent acquisition of Eastern Siberia and the prospect of national reunification growing greater every day, their disagreements have become too great to ignore. The co-rulers have agreed that the only way to settle this is to let the Russian people decide.

Shukshin is campaigning on a platform of reform and democracy, pledging to create a truly equal and free Russian Federation with a government elected by and subservient to the people before all else. Pokryshkin has opted for a more conservative approach, stating his commitment to democracy but reiterating that Russia is in need of a strong government capable of uniting and defending its people. Only time will tell which message is more popular.

directives.name: A Foundation for Research
directives.title: A Foundation for Research
directives.desc:
More than twenty years of civil war has, among many other things, all but destroyed the educational infrastructure of the nation, and led to the emigration or death of most competent scientists and physicists.

If we are to have any hope of continuing and completing our nuclear program, we must address this. We cannot wait for skilled scientists to make themselves known or return from afar, or for advanced institutes to be reclaimed. We must act.

We will directly fund the universities and research centers that we do have, and monitor them closely for students of loyalty and aptitude who can be directly recruited into our development program.

directives.name: Expand the Siberian Mines
directives.title: Expand the Siberian Mines
directives.desc:
Deep within Siberia lies Krasnoyarsk. Although important for other reasons, the region is also notable for possessing vast qualities of uranium deep below the surface. Uranium that we can now exploit.

In order to properly do so, an entire mining operation, and the infrastructure surrounding it, will have to be built from scratch. The effort required will be enormous, and the cost even greater, but such is irrelevant - we must have that uranium!

directives.name: Source Foreign Materials
directives.title: Source Foreign Materials
directives.desc:
If we cannot find enough uranium to support our program domestically, we shall have to look farther afield. Agents, legal and otherwise, will be dispatched across the world to research and investigate both known and rumored uranium deposits.

Whether we must buy the material, trade for it, or steal it, we will acquire it. The program must continue, and a bomb cares little for where the material inside it comes from.

directives.name: Spreading the SibPlan
directives.title: Spreading the SibPlan
directives.desc:
Before the war, Central Siberia was the site of one of the greatest planned industrial developments in history. The SibPlan transformed a backwards region into an industrial hub and a center of production. Our newly acquired eastern territories were mostly untouched by the SibPlan, and their miniscule industry pales in comparison to that of our heartland. The east must be brought up to standard.

We shall develop the Far East the same way the Soviets developed inland Siberia. A program of state-planned industrial projects will serve as the foundations for new production centers in the east. We will go further than the Soviets though. While their SibPlan was strictly managed by the state, ours will collaborate with our local corporations, helping establish strong private industry in the Far East.

directives.name: Expand the Volkomats
directives.title: Expand the Volkomats
directives.desc:
Controlling Siberia and the people who live in it has always been a challenge for past Russian governments, and it will no doubt be a challenge for us as well. This is made no easier by the fact that Eastern Siberia is now crawling with ex-military men who fought for one leader or another that now find themselves with nothing to do but grow bitter and resentful of our new rule. These men could be dangerous, but they also present an opportunity.

The Volkomats, our system of military commissariats, have proven successful in maintaining our control of the nation and keeping extremist organizations on the run. Expanding this system to encompass our new territory would help lock down the east. Recruiting disaffected army officers, black shirts, and NKVD agents into the Volkomats would give us a way to put the skills of these unpleasant people to work for us while placing them firmly under our control.

This is made no easier by the fact that Eastern Siberia is now crawling with ex-military men who fought for one leader or another that now find themselves with nothing to do but grow bitter and resentful of our new rule. These men could be dangerous, but they also present an opportunity.

The Volkomats, our system of military commissariats, have proven successful in maintaining our control of the nation and keeping extremist organizations on the run. Expanding this system to encompass our new territory would help lock down the east. Recruiting disaffected army officers, black shirts, and NKVD agents into the Volkomats would give us a way to put the skills of these unpleasant people to work for us while placing them firmly under our control.

directives.name: Winds of Change
directives.title: Winds of Change
directives.desc:
The people have spoken and their will is clear. After years of rule, Alexander Pokryshkin has finally tasted defeat at the ballot box, and Vasily Shukshin has been elected to lead the Federation forwards to a new, brighter future! Shukshin and his supporters have announced plans for a bold new wave of liberalization and reforms that they say will finally bring freedom and democracy to all of Russia.

While Shukshin's supporters are celebrating his victory, those who backed Pokryshkin's continued rule are already voicing their concerns. The leaders of the military have expressed reservations about a weakening of the central government, and the boards of Russia's new megacorporations expect it will be much more difficult to deal with a government that is truly beholden to the interests of the people. Let them complain all they like. They shall be the first tyrants to fall before the might of a free Russia, but not the last.

directives.name: Business as Usual
directives.title: Business as Usual
directives.desc:
In a result that surprised no one, the people of Russia have voted to continue Pokryshkin's reign as President of the Federation, picking his record of success and commitments to stability over Shukshin's radical promises of liberalization and weakened government. Acquisitions from the opposition of vote tampering and suppression have been widely dismissed by the media and the people, and the stage is set for the Siberian Falcon's rule to continue.

The President knows that this is no time for a weakened government and a divided people. Russia is still divided, and there are enemies within and without our borders who will work nonstop to tear down what we have built. The President will not let them. He has brought us this far, and the Russian people know that only he can lead them through what is to come. To change course now would only be to steer into a storm.

directives.name: Chase the Sun
directives.title: Chase the Sun
directives.desc:
Although it will be a long time before we have an operational nuclear weapon, we have successfully built the infrastructure necessary to ensure that we eventually will.

Our laboratories and research facilities are constructed and secured. Our educational institutions are turning out scientists with the necessary skills. Our agencies have secured both domestic and foreign sources of fissile material. All that is left is time.

When that day comes, and we complete our first nuclear test, we can take pride both in our accomplishments, and in the knowledge that Russia will, at long, long last, be free of outside interference.

directives.name: Funding the Central Design Bureau
directives.title: Funding the Central Design Bureau
directives.desc:
When Russia was fractured into dozens of warlords, the armies and pilots of Novosibirsk had only one advantage over their foes. While they could not match the numbers or fanaticism of their opponents, they knew they were always fighting with the best equipment Russia had to offer. This was solely because of the Central Design Bureau and the fantastic, innovative weaponry it produced.

The days of warlords are behind us but the bureau still proves its worth, its staff of designers, engineers, scientists, and entrepreneurs all working around the clock to make the next breakthrough that will change how wars are fought forever. We must increase our investment in the bureau, now that we have access to more wealth and resources than ever before. If they could create groundbreaking new aircraft on a shoestring budget, imagine what they will be able to do with the resources of all of Russia at their disposal.

directives.name: National Priority Projects
directives.title: National Priority Projects
directives.desc:
It is clear everywhere you look that Russia is rebuilding. Shops are opening, vacant buildings are being filled and new ones are being built. Shelves are fully stocked for the first time ever and the people are going back to work, but there is still much to do. We have come far, but there is still a long way to go before Russia is fully ready to retake its place on the modern global stage. It is our duty as the Motherland's government to help her get there.

To assist the recovery and rebuilding efforts, four programs have been selected for government funding and support. Dubbed the 'National Priority Projects' by the media, they focus on improving public health, access to education, housing availability and quality, and agricultural development. By supporting improvements in these four vital areas we are progressing towards a point where Russia is not just reunified, but rebuilt and prosperous at last.

directives.name: Our Eastern Bastion
directives.title: Our Eastern Bastion
directives.desc:
The port city of Magadan used to be so insignificant it didn't even appear on maps of eastern Russia. During the decades of anarchy, it became important because it was Russia's largest unoccupied port, but even then, after years of improvements made by the various warlords who have controlled it, it is still barely up to the task of serving as our primary port.

Rebuilding Russia will require doing significant amounts of trading and business with the nations of the world, and our ability to trade with them is limited by our port's capacity. Both business and government officials have been urging us to invest more into Magadan, and to complete its transformation into Russia's new doorstep to the world. Ask and they shall receive. Magadan will become worthy of the responsibility thrust upon it, and we shall finally have full, unfettered access to the global marketplace.

directives.name: A Disciplined Force
directives.title: A Disciplined Force
directives.desc:
Our military is one of the best in Russia. Our reunification of Siberia is proof enough of that for anyone. But being the best in Russia does not mean we are ready to take on the world. So far, our military has fought bandits and warlords, and semi-industrialized regional rivals, but we have yet to take on a full, modern, and war-ready military power, and considering the dangerous state of the world, we may have to sooner than we'd like.

The technological gap between our forces and those of the Germans and the Japanese is shrinking, due to the heroic efforts of our design bureaus, but technology alone does not make a modern army. It does not matter how good the gun is if the man is too afraid to fire it. Our army is not a disorganized rabble, but its discipline still leaves room for improvement. We will see that these improvements are made, and our men are refined into hardened warriors, ready for the conflicts ahead.

directives.name: Demokratizatsiya
directives.title: Demokratizatsiya
directives.desc:
Shukshin's victory is a triumph for the cause of Russian freedom, but it is only the first step on the road towards democracy. Pokryshkin and his toadies spent years building up their powers and doing their damndest to turn Russia into a one-party state once more. Undoing their efforts will take time, and we must begin with small reforms to prepare the nation for the great changes it has in store.

Soon, the government will launch a new initiative called "Demokratizatsiya" - Democratization. Starting at the local level, the people of Russia will now be able to elect their leaders and representatives. Once a sufficient permanent election structure is in place, we will be able to organize regularly scheduled elections at last. Other early reforms will include passing term limits and preparing to implement a separation of powers among the various departments of government.

directives.name: Curb the Corporations
directives.title: Curb the Corporations
directives.desc:
A new piece of legislation has been introduced recently that would put in place some token limitations on the activities of the corporations. The limits are trivial at best and mostly have to do with implementing the bare minimum of government oversight on stock trading, but the proposed law has still attracted significant attention from the people and the corporations for one reason. It used to be the case that legislation like this would be shot down immediately before even going to a vote, but this is no longer the case.

President Shukshin will place his full support behind this law, and encourage his supporters to do the same. On paper, it really is little more than a token effort, but it will signal to the whole nation that Shukshin is no crony of the corporations. We may not be able to end their influence right away, but we can make it clear to the world that the days of Russian companies exploiting Russian people for foreign money will soon be over.

directives.name: Entrench Our Position
directives.title: Entrench Our Position
directives.desc:
In many ways the election was a gamble, a test to see if the President's popularity could overcome his reputation as an authoritarian leader, and to see if the party's position was strong enough to stand up to an election we (mostly) avoided tampering in. The institutions held, but in some places just barely. The vote was closer than we liked, and there is work to be done before the next round of elections eventually come around.

Districts and voting precincts must be redrawn to better represent the loyal citizens of the Federation and avoid empowering radical elements. Stricter voter ID laws must be put in place to clamp down on rampant voter fraud in certain regions. Even the process for filing as a candidate must be revisited to make sure only candidates registered with approved parties can run. The party will not be put in a situation where it could be overtaken by radicals again.

The institutions held, but in some places just barely. The vote was closer than we liked, and there is work to be done before the next round of elections eventually come around.

Districts and voting precincts must be redrawn to better represent the loyal citizens of the Federation and avoid empowering radical elements. Stricter voter ID laws must be put in place to clamp down on rampant voter fraud in certain regions. Even the process for filing as a candidate must be revisited to make sure only candidates registered with approved parties can run. The party will not be put in a situation where it could be overtaken by radicals again.

directives.name: Lucrative Contracts
directives.title: Lucrative Contracts
directives.desc:
Eastern Siberia may be an underdeveloped region, but if you look below the surface it is teeming with wealth in the form of valuable resources and minerals. Even more important in the modern era is its stockpile of human resources. Millions of Russians live in our newly acquired eastern territories, each of them a potential consumer. The corporations are practically salivating to get permission from the government to expand their operations to the Far East, and we have a chance to profit off of their enthusiasm.

A new round of government contracts in the Far East will expand the reach of our loyal and helpful corporations, firmly entrenching Russia's greatest companies on the global financial stage. Incentivized private investment will also help develop Russia's sparsest region. Last, but certainly not least, we will make an ungodly amount of money on the contract bidding.

directives.name: Towards a Glorious Future
directives.title: Towards a Glorious Future
directives.desc:
To be Russian these days is to watch destiny unfold before your eyes. It is to see a nation rising from the ashes like a phoenix, born from the most unlikely of embers. No one could have guessed an ace pilot leading a ragtag band of military men and disaffected local politicians would establish the next government of Russia? Who would have guessed a warlord army operating out of Novosibirsk would reunite the entirety of eastern Russia? Against the odds, the Federation has persisted, and now it stands triumphant, its final victory drawing near.

To be Russian these days is to stand at the middle point of a long road. Behind you are the decades of suffering and violence that have been overcome. Ahead lies great uncertainty, and the potential for conflict to put all of the hardships of the past to shame. But there is also the potential for something brighter, something better. Russia has come so far so quickly. The only thing left to do is keep pushing forwards, to whatever lies at the end of the road.

directives.name: Dreams of Federation
directives.title: Dreams of Federation
directives.desc:
When it was originally conceived, the Russian Federation was supposed to be Russia's best chance at democracy. The idealism of the Central Siberian Republic was always doomed to failure, but the Federation could provide a practical, reasonable alternative that would reunite the Russian lands and peoples and secure a future defined by freedom and stability. What it morphed into under Pokryshkin's rule was a bastardized, authoritarian imitation of the original goal, but the damage can still be undone.

Slowly, surely, the people of Russia are starting to wake up. They are realizing that this new President's promises are not false, and his words are not empty. The Russian Federation really can be a nation of practical democracy rather than corrupt authoritarianism. After decades of bitter winters, spring is coming to the Motherland.

directives.name: The Guiding Hand
directives.title: The Guiding Hand
directives.desc:
Only a few years ago Russia was a land of weakness, ruled by petty mewling warlords more concerned with pillaging their motherland than rebuilding it. It took men with vision, strength, and persistence to put a stop to this, but the time of weakness is done. Pokryshkin and his allies have vanquished the traitors, radicals, and anyone else who stood in the way of a united Russian Federation, and now they shall finish the job and reunite Russia once and for all.

No more will the peoples of the Motherland fight against one another, divided by harmful political ideologies and crippled by tyrannical invaders. Under the strong and unquestioned leadership of President Pokryshkin, the citizens of Russia stand as one against any who would try to stop their progress. Without his leadership, they know none of this would be possible. Without his guidance, they know no further success could be had. How lucky then, that when Russia needs him most, Pokryshkin is here to lead the way.

NOV_the_siberian_mandate.name: The Siberian Mandate
NOV_the_siberian_mandate.title: The Siberian Mandate
NOV_the_siberian_mandate.desc:
After years of struggle the unthinkable has been achieved. The vastness of Siberia has been reunified under one flag. Securing this much of Russia has been no easy feat. To secure our hold we have had to fight off every devil of Russia's past, from monarchists fanatics to fascist thugs to Soviet holdouts. We have vanquished them all and we now stand triumphant as the masters of the east and the rightful government of all of Russia.

The conquest of Siberia has taken its toll on us. Russia remains fractured but even now we are already one of the largest nations on earth, and administering a territory this massive requires a strong and stable government. We should take this opportunity to secure our hold and ensure that our administration is prepared for the tasks that lie ahead. The final reunification with the west is near, one way or another. We will not be caught unprepared.

RUS_SIB_nukes_into_the_atomic_age.name: Into the Atomic Age
RUS_SIB_nukes_into_the_atomic_age.title: Into the Atomic Age
RUS_SIB_nukes_into_the_atomic_age.desc:
Russia has long been regarded, by powers near and far, as a backwater, a vast steppe full of peasant farmers, and decades of revolution, collapse, and civil war has done little to challenge this perception. But this will soon change.

With the resources, human and otherwise, that we have acquired during our campaigns of re-unification, we possess the ability to begin a nuclear program.

The power of the atom is a great equalizer in the game of geopolitics, and we shall now act to harness it for ourselves.

NOV_root_out_the_remnants.name: Root Out the Remnants
NOV_root_out_the_remnants.title: Root Out the Remnants
NOV_root_out_the_remnants.desc:
The Russian people are grateful to have a strong, democratic government ruling over them at last, but there are still a few troublemakers who wish to overthrow us. These various extremists, whether they be fascists or communists or anarchists or monarchists, are all unified by their hatred for our government. These radicals held low enough profiles to be missed by the first round of crackdowns and arrests we made whenever we defeated their bosses, but now they have returned to make trouble and we must put a stop to it.

There is no reason to assume what worked before won't work again. A combination of surveillance, sabotage, arrests, and anti-radical propaganda will be enough to cripple the various terrorist societies that have cropped up across Siberia and turn the public firmly against their divisive messages.

NOV_consolidate_the_new_territories.name: Consolidate the New Territories
NOV_consolidate_the_new_territories.title: Consolidate the New Territories
NOV_consolidate_the_new_territories.desc:
It is almost impossible to explain just how vast and sparsely populated Siberia is. Outside of a few urban centers like Irkutsk and Novosibirsk, it is millions of square kilometers of wilderness and scattered villages. This is especially true of the newly integrated eastern regions. Even the Tsars and the Soviets never fully extended their administrations over this region, and the eastern warlords never came close to matching what they did accomplish. The task of integrating this territory has been left to us.

The urban centers of the east will form a nucleus of a new administrative web that will cover all of Eastern Siberia. Every town and village, every isolated hamlet, all of them will be assigned to districts and administrative regions, and each will have administrators and politicians appointed to oversee them and represent them within our government. No more will the Far East be an isolated backwater forgotten by the Russian government. It is an integral part of the Russian nation, and it will be treated as such.

NOV_reaffirm_our_commitments.name: Reaffirm Our Commitments
NOV_reaffirm_our_commitments.title: Reaffirm Our Commitments
NOV_reaffirm_our_commitments.desc:
With the sudden expansion of our territory and our associated advance on the world stage, eyes across the world are studying us, watching for our next move to see what it signals. We must show them that we are still the same government they have learned to trust. Our impending reunification of Russia has not changed any of our agreements, and we are still happy to do business with the other nations of the world.

The acquisition of Russia's longest coastline and several developed ports has made the matter of trade much easier. The nations and companies who have already invested in Russia are excitedly offering to expand operations further. Meanwhile from Tokyo to Washington we have gained the attention of government and business alike. It is time to double down on our message while everyone is watching: Russia is open for business.

RUS_SIB_nukes_establish_closed_facilitie.name: Establish Closed Facilities
RUS_SIB_nukes_establish_closed_facilitie.title: Establish Closed Facilities
RUS_SIB_nukes_establish_closed_facilitie.desc:
Just as we are desperate to unlock the secrets of the atom, our enemies are equally desperate to prevent us from doing so. Although there are many ways to increase security, very few are absolute, and absolute security is necessary when the stakes are so high.

We will therefore sequester our entire nuclear program - laboratories, enrichment facilities, reactors, and production lines - in closed cities. These cities will not permit entry or exit to anyone without direct authorization from the highest levels of government.

Although cumbersome and expensive, such is irrelevant. We must have safety and security for the program, and we will.

RUS_SIB_nukes_address_the_uranium_proble.title: Address the Uranium Problem
RUS_SIB_nukes_address_the_uranium_proble.desc:
Russia is a truly enormous land, possessing many varied resources in vast abundance. Unfortunately, however, uranium is not one of those, so far as we know. Without a steady and reliable supply of uranium, we will have no program, and thus no bomb.

We must therefore make every effort in order to find this supply as soon as possible. No matter what it costs, we must find new sources of fissile material.

NOV_election_season.name: Election Season
NOV_election_season.title: Election Season
NOV_election_season.desc:
It is no secret that the co-rulers of our nation do not get along. Publicly, Pokryshkin and Shukshin present a united front, but it is well known that they have agreed on little for years. The two men have been able to set aside their differences and cooperate up until now, but with the recent acquisition of Eastern Siberia and the prospect of national reunification growing greater every day, their disagreements have become too great to ignore. The co-rulers have agreed that the only way to settle this is to let the Russian people decide.

Shukshin is campaigning on a platform of reform and democracy, pledging to create a truly equal and free Russian Federation with a government elected by and subservient to the people before all else. Pokryshkin has opted for a more conservative approach, stating his commitment to democracy but reiterating that Russia is in need of a strong government capable of uniting and defending its people. Only time will tell which message is more popular.

RUS_SIB_nukes_a_foundation_for_research.name: A Foundation for Research
RUS_SIB_nukes_a_foundation_for_research.title: A Foundation for Research
RUS_SIB_nukes_a_foundation_for_research.desc:
More than twenty years of civil war has, among many other things, all but destroyed the educational infrastructure of the nation, and led to the emigration or death of most competent scientists and physicists.

If we are to have any hope of continuing and completing our nuclear program, we must address this. We cannot wait for skilled scientists to make themselves known or return from afar, or for advanced institutes to be reclaimed. We must act.

We will directly fund the universities and research centers that we do have, and monitor them closely for students of loyalty and aptitude who can be directly recruited into our development program.

RUS_SIB_nukes_expand_the_siberian_mines.title: Expand the Siberian Mines
RUS_SIB_nukes_expand_the_siberian_mines.desc:
Deep within Siberia lies Krasnoyarsk. Although important for other reasons, the region is also notable for possessing vast qualities of uranium deep below the surface. Uranium that we can now exploit.

In order to properly do so, an entire mining operation, and the infrastructure surrounding it, will have to be built from scratch. The effort required will be enormous, and the cost even greater, but such is irrelevant - we must have that uranium!

NOV_spreading_the_sibplan.name: Spreading the SibPlan
NOV_spreading_the_sibplan.title: Spreading the SibPlan
NOV_spreading_the_sibplan.desc:
Before the war, Central Siberia was the site of one of the greatest planned industrial developments in history. The SibPlan transformed a backwards region into an industrial hub and a center of production. Our newly acquired eastern territories were mostly untouched by the SibPlan, and their miniscule industry pales in comparison to that of our heartland. The east must be brought up to standard.

We shall develop the Far East the same way the Soviets developed inland Siberia. A program of state-planned industrial projects will serve as the foundations for new production centers in the east. We will go further than the Soviets though. While their SibPlan was strictly managed by the state, ours will collaborate with our local corporations, helping establish strong private industry in the Far East.

NOV_expand_the_voenkomats.name: Expand the Volkomats
NOV_expand_the_voenkomats.title: Expand the Volkomats
NOV_expand_the_voenkomats.desc:
Controlling Siberia and the people who live in it has always been a challenge for past Russian governments, and it will no doubt be a challenge for us as well. This is made no easier by the fact that Eastern Siberia is now crawling with ex-military men who fought for one leader or another that now find themselves with nothing to do but grow bitter and resentful of our new rule. These men could be dangerous, but they also present an opportunity.

The Volkomats, our system of military commissariats, have proven successful in maintaining our control of the nation and keeping extremist organizations on the run. Expanding this system to encompass our new territory would help lock down the east. Recruiting disaffected army officers, black shirts, and NKVD agents into the Volkomats would give us a way to put the skills of these unpleasant people to work for us while placing them firmly under our control.

NOV_winds_of_change.name: Winds of Change
NOV_winds_of_change.title: Winds of Change
NOV_winds_of_change.desc:
The people have spoken and their will is clear. After years of rule, Alexander Pokryshkin has finally tasted defeat at the ballot box, and Vasily Shukshin has been elected to lead the Federation forwards to a new, brighter future! Shukshin and his supporters have announced plans for a bold new wave of liberalization and reforms that they say will finally bring freedom and democracy to all of Russia.

While Shukshin's supporters are celebrating his victory, those who backed Pokryshkin's continued rule are already voicing their concerns. The leaders of the military have expressed reservations about a weakening of the central government, and the boards of Russia's new megacorporations expect it will be much more difficult to deal with a government that is truly beholden to the interests of the people. Let them complain all they like. They shall be the first tyrants to fall before the might of a free Russia, but not the last.

NOV_business_as_usual.name: Business as Usual
NOV_business_as_usual.title: Business as Usual
NOV_business_as_usual.desc:
In a result that surprised no one, the people of Russia have voted to continue Pokryshkin's reign as President of the Federation, picking his record of success and commitments to stability over Shukshin's radical promises of liberalization and weakened government. Acquisitions from the opposition of vote tampering and suppression have been widely dismissed by the media and the people, and the stage is set for the Siberian Falcon's rule to continue.

The President knows that this is no time for a weakened government and a divided people. Russia is still divided, and there are enemies within and without our borders who will work nonstop to tear down what we have built. The President will not let them. He has brought us this far, and the Russian people know that only he can lead them through what is to come. To change course now would only be to steer into a storm.

RUS_SIB_nukes_chasing_the_sun.title: Chase the Sun
RUS_SIB_nukes_chasing_the_sun.desc:

When that day comes, and we complete our first nuclear test, we can take pride both in our accomplishments, and in the knowledge that Russia will, at long, long last, be free of outside interference.

NOV_funding_the_central_design_bureau.title: Funding the Central Design Bureau
NOV_funding_the_central_design_bureau.desc:
When Russia was fractured into dozens of warlords, the armies and pilots of Novosibirsk had only one advantage over their foes. While they could not match the numbers or fanaticism of their opponents, they knew they were always fighting with the best equipment Russia had to offer. This was solely because of the Central Design Bureau and the fantastic, innovative weaponry it produced.

NOV_national_priority_projects.name: National Priority Projects
NOV_national_priority_projects.title: National Priority Projects
NOV_national_priority_projects.desc:
It is clear everywhere you look that Russia is rebuilding. Shops are opening, vacant buildings are being filled and new ones are being built. Shelves are fully stocked for the first time ever and the people are going back to work, but there is still much to do. We have come far, but there is still a long way to go before Russia is fully ready to retake its place on the modern global stage. Dubbed the 'National Priority Projects' by the media, they focus on improving public health, access to education, housing availability and quality, and agricultural development. By supporting improvements in these four vital areas we are progressing towards a point where Russia is not just reunified, but rebuilt and prosperous at last.

NOV_our_eastern_bastion.name: Our Eastern Bastion
NOV_our_eastern_bastion.title: Our Eastern Bastion
NOV_our_eastern_bastion.desc:
The port city of Magadan used to be so insignificant it didn't even appear on maps of eastern Russia. During the decades of anarchy, it became important because it was Russia's largest unoccupied port, but even then, after years of improvements made by the various warlords who have controlled it, it is still barely up to the task of serving as our primary port.

Rebuilding Russia will require doing significant amounts of trading and business with the nations of the world, and our ability to trade with them is limited by our port's capacity. Both business and government officials have been urging us to invest more into Magadan, and to complete its transformation into Russia's new doorstep to the world. Ask and they shall receive. Magadan will become worthy of the responsibility thrust upon it, and we shall finally have full, unfettered access to the global marketplace.

NOV_a_disciplined_force.name: A Disciplined Force
NOV_a_disciplined_force.title: A Disciplined Force
NOV_a_disciplined_force.desc:
Our military is one of the best in Russia. Our reunification of Siberia is proof enough of that for anyone. But being the best in Russia does not mean we are ready to take on the world. So far, our military has fought bandits and warlords, and semi-industrialized regional rivals, but we have yet to take on a full, modern, and war-ready military power, and considering the dangerous state of the world, we may have to sooner than we'd like.

The technological gap between our forces and those of the Germans and the Japanese is shrinking, due to the heroic efforts of our design bureaus, but technology alone does not make a modern army. It does not matter how good the gun is if the man is too afraid to fire it. Our army is not a disorganized rabble, but its discipline still leaves room for improvement. We will see that these improvements are made, and our men are refined into hardened warriors, ready for the conflicts ahead.

NOV_demokratizatsiya.name: Demokratizatsiya
NOV_demokratizatsiya.title: Demokratizatsiya
NOV_demokratizatsiya.desc:
Shukshin's victory is a triumph for the cause of Russian freedom, but it is only the first step on the road towards democracy. Pokryshkin and his toadies spent years building up their powers and doing their damndest to turn Russia into a one-party state once more. Undoing their efforts will take time, and we must begin with small reforms to prepare the nation for the great changes it has in store.

Soon, the government will launch a new initiative called "Demokratizatsiya" - Democratization. Starting at the local level, the people of Russia will now be able to elect their leaders and representatives. Once a sufficient permanent election structure is in place, we will be able to organize regularly scheduled elections at last. Other early reforms will include passing term limits and preparing to implement a separation of powers among the various departments of government.

NOV_curb_the_corporations.name: Curb the Corporations
NOV_curb_the_corporations.title: Curb the Corporations
NOV_curb_the_corporations.desc:
A new piece of legislation has been introduced recently that would put in place some token limitations on the activities of the corporations. The limits are trivial at best and mostly have to do with implementing the bare minimum of government oversight on stock trading, but the proposed law has still attracted significant attention from the people and the corporations for one reason. It used to be the case that legislation like this would be shot down immediately before even going to a vote, but this is no longer the case.

President Shukshin will place his full support behind this law, and encourage his supporters to do the same. On paper, it really is little more than a token effort, but it will signal to the whole nation that Shukshin is no crony of the corporations. We may not be able to end their influence right away, but we can make it clear to the world that the days of Russian companies exploiting Russian people for foreign money will soon be over.

NOV_entrench_our_position.name: Entrench Our Position
NOV_entrench_our_position.title: Entrench Our Position
NOV_entrench_our_position.desc:
In many ways the election was a gamble, a test to see if the President's popularity could overcome his reputation as an authoritarian leader, and to see if the party's position was strong enough to stand up to an election we (mostly) avoided tampering in. The institutions held, but in some places just barely. The vote was closer than we liked, and there is work to be done before the next round of elections eventually come around.

Districts and voting precincts must be redrawn to better represent the loyal citizens of the Federation and avoid empowering radical elements. Stricter voter ID laws must be put in place to clamp down on rampant voter fraud in certain regions. Even the process for filing as a candidate must be revisited to make sure only candidates registered with approved parties can run. The party will not be put in a situation where it could be overtaken by radicals again.

NOV_lucrative_contracts.name: Lucrative Contracts
NOV_lucrative_contracts.title: Lucrative Contracts
NOV_lucrative_contracts.desc:
Eastern Siberia may be an underdeveloped region, but if you look below the surface it is teeming with wealth in the form of valuable resources and minerals. Even more important in the modern era is its stockpile of human resources. Millions of Russians live in our newly acquired eastern territories, each of them a potential consumer. The corporations are practically salivating to get permission from the government to expand their operations to the Far East, and we have a chance to profit off of their enthusiasm.

A new round of government contracts in the Far East will expand the reach of our loyal and helpful corporations, firmly entrenching Russia's greatest companies on the global financial stage. Incentivized private investment will also help develop Russia's sparsest region. Last, but certainly not least, we will make an ungodly amount of money on the contract bidding.

NOV_towards_a_glorious_future.name: Towards a Glorious Future
NOV_towards_a_glorious_future.title: Towards a Glorious Future
NOV_towards_a_glorious_future.desc:
To be Russian these days is to watch destiny unfold before your eyes. It is to see a nation rising from the ashes like a phoenix, born from the most unlikely of embers. No one could have guessed an ace pilot leading a ragtag band of military men and disaffected local politicians would establish the next government of Russia? Who would have guessed a warlord army operating out of Novosibirsk would reunite the entirety of eastern Russia? Against the odds, the Federation has persisted, and now it stands triumphant, its final victory drawing near.

To be Russian these days is to stand at the middle point of a long road. Behind you are the decades of suffering and violence that have been overcome. Ahead lies great uncertainty, and the potential for conflict to put all of the hardships of the past to shame. But there is also the potential for something brighter, something better. Russia has come so far so quickly. The only thing left to do is keep pushing forwards, to whatever lies at the end of the road.

NOV_dreams_of_federation.name: Dreams of Federation
NOV_dreams_of_federation.title: Dreams of Federation
NOV_dreams_of_federation.desc:
When it was originally conceived, the Russian Federation was supposed to be Russia's best chance at democracy. The idealism of the Central Siberian Republic was always doomed to failure, but the Federation could provide a practical, reasonable alternative that would reunite the Russian lands and peoples and secure a future defined by freedom and stability. What it morphed into under Pokryshkin's rule was a bastardized, authoritarian imitation of the original goal, but the damage can still be undone.

Slowly, surely, the people of Russia are starting to wake up. They are realizing that this new President's promises are not false, and his words are not empty. The Russian Federation really can be a nation of practical democracy rather than corrupt authoritarianism. After decades of bitter winters, spring is coming to the Motherland.

The idealism of the Central Siberian Republic was always doomed to failure, but the Federation could provide a practical, reasonable alternative that would reunite the Russian lands and peoples and secure a future defined by freedom and stability. What it morphed into under Pokryshkin's rule was a bastardized, authoritarian imitation of the original goal, but the damage can still be undone.

Slowly, surely, the people of Russia are starting to wake up. They are realizing that this new President's promises are not false, and his words are not empty. The Russian Federation really can be a nation of practical democracy rather than corrupt authoritarianism. After decades of bitter winters, spring is coming to the Motherland.

NOV_the_guiding_hand.name: The Guiding Hand
NOV_the_guiding_hand.title: The Guiding Hand
NOV_the_guiding_hand.desc:
Only a few years ago Russia was a land of weakness, ruled by petty mewling warlords more concerned with pillaging their motherland than rebuilding it. It took men with vision, strength, and persistence to put a stop to this, but the time of weakness is done. Pokryshkin and his allies have vanquished the traitors, radicals, and anyone else who stood in the way of a united Russian Federation, and now they shall finish the job and reunite Russia once and for all.

No more will the peoples of the Motherland fight against one another, divided by harmful political ideologies and crippled by tyrannical invaders. Under the strong and unquestioned leadership of President Pokryshkin, the citizens of Russia stand as one against any who would try to stop their progress. Without his leadership, they know none of this would be possible. Without his guidance, they know no further success could be had. How lucky then, that when Russia needs him most, Pokryshkin is here to lead the way.
